clue.text: Sacrifice two small boys

parts.note: Vic and Tim are short forms of the boys' names Victor and Timothy, giving two pieces
Vic and Tim are short forms of the boys' names Victor and Timothy, giving two pieces

explanation.surface: A grim image of two little lads being offered up as a sacrifice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' signals that the boys' names are shortened forms: VIC (Victor) and TIM (Timothy).
explanation.definitionFit: A sacrifice, as a noun, is the creature offered up and killed, a sense now usually expressed by the synonym for one who suffers.

clue.text: Force emperor to go by rail

parts.note: IMP is the abbreviation of Imperator, Latin for emperor, seen on Roman coins
EL is the elevated railway, as in Chicago's El, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: An emperor being made to travel by train rather than in state.
explanation.definitionFit: To force someone to act is to drive or urge them on, a close verb synonym.

clue.text: Distressed people involved in unlawful action at England's borders

indicators.note: being involved in something puts these people within the legal wrong

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong, an unlawful act for which one can be sued
men is a common crossword stand-in for people

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters, here from England's

explanation.surface: People caught up in some illegal act at the English frontier, and upset about it.
explanation.walkthrough: A tort is a civil wrong under English law, as opposed to a crime; 'involved in' puts the people inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone distressed is in mental anguish, which is what being plagued or racked by suffering means.

clue.text: Being in the A-team is happily an accident

indicators.note: the answer is being, or existing, inside the run of words A-team is happily

explanation.surface: Someone happily finding themselves in the first team, though only by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'teaM IS HAPpily'.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor unlucky event, a mishap, is a small accident or misfortune.

clue.text: Team gets a thrill from partner

parts.note: a side is a team, as in a football side
a kick is a thrill, as in getting a kick out of something

explanation.surface: A team member gets excitement from playing alongside a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidekick is a close companion or junior associate, an informal synonym for a partner.

clue.text: The doc struggled with eyestrain for a very long time

indicators.note: letters that struggled are wrestling about into a new order, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor battling with sore eyes for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: THEDOC and EYESTRAIN together make the fifteen letters. 'Since the year dot' is a British idiom for 'from time immemorial'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means from the earliest times one can remember, hence over an extremely lengthy period.

clue.text: Make fun of candidate at the back following report of record recount

indicators.note: following places the teasing word and the last letter after the sound of record
a report is something heard, so the word for record is given by its sound

parts.note: a disc is a record, as in a vinyl disc
to rib someone is to tease or make fun of them

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter, here of candidate

explanation.surface: Mocking an election candidate during a vote recount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report of' is a sound signal: 'disc' said aloud. 'recount' looks like part of the election picture but is the definition, meaning narrate.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount is to tell or narrate events, and to describe is likewise to give an account of them.

clue.text: Does away with unoriginal talents

indicators.note: not original here means without its origin, the opening letter of the word for talents

parts.note: skills are talents or abilities

explanation.surface: Someone stamps out talents that lack originality.
explanation.definitionFit: To do away with someone is to murder or slay them, an idiom for the same act.

clue.text: Restrict arguments against school

parts.note: cons are arguments against, as in pros and cons
to school someone is to train or teach them

explanation.surface: Limiting the case against a school.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrict is to hold back or limit, which is what forcing within bounds means.

clue.text: Fights to limit European reserves

indicators.note: to limit is to hem in, so the word for fights encloses the letter

parts.note: spars means fights or boxes, as in sparring

explanation.surface: Bouts of fighting kept in check by European reserve forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare items or players are extras held back, which is what reserves are.

clue.text: A safe place to hang about without doubt snuggling up

parts.note: a nest is a safe, snug home

indicators.note: without means the hesitation sound is taken out

parts.note: to linger is to hang about or loiter
er is the sound of hesitation or doubt

explanation.surface: Seeking a safe spot to loiter, snuggling up with no qualms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without doubt' looks like an idiom meaning certainly; here 'doubt' is ER, removed from LINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Nestling means settling cosily against someone, the same as snuggling up.

clue.text: Turn off beer with tips of Indian tea mixed in

indicators.note: mixed in says the jumbled letters go inside the beer

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

indicators.note: mixed means the letters I, N and tea are stirred into a new order
the tips of a word are its two ends, here of Indian

explanation.surface: Putting someone off by lacing their beer with Indian tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn off' is the definition in its sense of putting someone off, not switching something off; 'mixed' is the anagram signal for the tips plus tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn someone off is to make them lose interest or sympathy, which is to estrange or repel them.

clue.text: Sister screwed up second chances

indicators.note: something screwed up is crumpled or messed up, so the word's letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A sister who failed gets another go at the exams.
explanation.definitionFit: Resits are exams taken again after failing, giving candidates a second chance.

clue.text: Awkward situation about first son

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: top means first or best, as in top of the class
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A tricky moment concerning a first-born boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a spot is to be in a tight corner or difficult position.

clue.text: Go on trying for a split vote on the right

parts.note: per means for a, as in pounds per hour
to sever is to split or cut apart

indicators.note: the rightmost letter of the word vote is the one taken

explanation.surface: Keep pushing for a divided vote among right-wingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the right' looks like a political label but picks the final letter E of vote.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to keep going despite difficulty, which is to keep on trying.

clue.text: Husband regularly unable to follow a small part of routine

indicators.note: to follow places the picked letters after the small part

parts.note: a bit is a small part or piece

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of unable is taken

explanation.surface: A husband who can never manage his small part of the daily routine.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of 'unable' give UAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Routine, as an adjective, describes something done by custom every time, which is what habitual means.

clue.text: Opening there should collapse without EU

indicators.note: collapsing letters fall into disorder, so these words are rearranged
without says the letters of EU are left out of the jumble

explanation.surface: A political prediction that a gap will open if Britain leaves the European Union.
explanation.walkthrough: Take THERESHOULD, remove one E and the U, and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A threshold is a doorway or entrance, so it is an opening in a literal sense.

clue.text: Willing to follow orders initially and be on strange new diet

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of orders
strange signals that N and diet are scrambled into an odd order

explanation.surface: A dutiful dieter who follows instructions and takes up an odd new regime.
explanation.walkthrough: N and DIET rearranged give DIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An obedient person complies with instructions, so is ready and willing to follow.

clue.text: Clubs are confident about backing bid in a convincing manner

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for are confident surrounds the turned bid

parts.note: to rely on something is to be confident in it

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so bid is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Card players confident in supporting a bid, making it sound convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something credibly means doing it believably, so as to convince others.

clue.text: Extremely right-wing group of people

indicators.note: only the extremes of the word are kept: its first two and last two letters, the middle dropped

explanation.surface: A far-right political faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' here keeps two letters at each extreme of 'right-wing': RI and NG.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring is a circle of people working together, often secretly, like a spy or smuggling gang.

clue.text: Clear river flows into a bay

indicators.note: a river flowing into a bay goes inside it, so the letter is put within

parts.note: a bight is a wide curving bay, like the Great Australian Bight

explanation.surface: A clean river running into a bay.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear weather or light is sunny and luminous, which is what bright describes.

clue.text: Ridiculed time to relax before starting degree

indicators.note: before says the relaxing word comes ahead of the letter from degree

parts.note: to ease is to relax or slacken

indicators.note: starting picks the first letter of degree

explanation.surface: A student mocked for taking time off before beginning a degree course.
explanation.definitionFit: To be teased is to be mocked playfully, so ridiculed is a near synonym.

clue.text: Take off football kit

definitions.meaning: a team's ... is its playing kit of shirt, shorts and socks, a British usage

explanation.surface: Pulling off one's football gear after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a football team's strip is its uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for removing clothing and a British noun for a team's outfit.

clue.text: A supporter's unbounded naivety is grating

parts.note: a bra is a supporter, and the 's adds an S

indicators.note: unbounded strips the boundaries, two letters off each end of naivety

explanation.surface: A backer's boundless innocence gets on everyone's nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unbounded' removes NA and TY from naivety, leaving IVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something grating is harsh and irritating, as is an abrasive manner or a rough, scraping surface.

clue.text: Absent-minded doctor gave up but not quietly

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are reworked
but not says the letter for quietly is left out of the jumble

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction meaning quietly

explanation.surface: A forgetful doctor who quietly gave up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being absent-minded means being distracted and unfocused, much like having a hazy, unclear mind.

clue.text: Get close to a possibly brief death

indicators.note: possibly says the word brief could be arranged in some other way

parts.note: end means death, as in meet one's end

explanation.surface: Getting near to what may be a swift death.
explanation.definitionFit: To get close to someone is to make friends with them, forming a bond.

clue.text: Befuddled with drink provided by heartless bloke

parts.note: grog is a drink of spirits and water, or slang for alcohol

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the word for bloke is removed

parts.note: a guy is a bloke or man

explanation.surface: A man confused with booze, supplied by a cold-hearted fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Groggy means dazed or unsteady, as if from drink or sleep, so it is a synonym of confused.

clue.text: Continue to be up to no good for 14

definitions.note: the definition is the answer to 14 down, meaning go on trying

parts.note: to keep doing something is to continue it

parts.words: to be up to no good
parts.note: to be at it is to be up to mischief, a British informal phrase

explanation.surface: Continuing to misbehave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At it' is informal British for 'up to no good'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to carry on working at something without giving up, the sense of the 14 down answer.

clue.text: After a fashion I tried to become more presentable

indicators.note: after a fashion means in some other manner, so the letters of I tried are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who made a half-hearted effort to look smarter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidier means neater and better kept, so more fit to be seen.
